quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: Two drivers arrive at the same time at a four-way stop sign. Who goes first?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver can go without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, give the right-of-way to the driver on your right if you both arrive at the same time. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, what should you do?

options.text: Let pedestrians cross first.
Speed up as fast as you can.
Back up slowly.
Wait for another driver to wave you forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go. But first, check for pedestrians and other traffic still in the intersection and let them cross.

questions.question: What causes most traffic crashes?

options.text: New drivers.
Driver mistakes.
Bad weather.
Bad roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driver mistakes.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do not see other vehicles or act unexpectedly. Communicate with other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: Where are stop lines (solid white lines) painted on roads?

options.text: On curves and hills.
Near churches and schools.
At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
On freeway on-ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They show drivers exactly where to stop.

questions.question: Why is night driving more dangerous?

options.text: Traffic moves faster at night.
There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
More accidents happen at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: It is dark at night, so drivers cannot see as well as during the day. Use your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or whenever you cannot see 500 feet ahead.

questions.question: You are in a line of traffic crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates. What should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way. You don't need to check for trains.
You can pass slower drivers while crossing the tracks.
Make sure your vehicle has enough space to cross without stopping.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle has enough space to cross without stopping.
questions.explanation: Check that you have enough room to cross the tracks completely before starting. Never pass other vehicles at railroad crossings. Always check for trains before crossing.

questions.question: A police officer motions you through a red light. What should you do?

options.text: Wait for the light to turn green.
Go through the red light as the officer directed.
Ask the officer for instructions.
Assume the officer doesn't see the red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the red light as the officer directed.
questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer's directions. They override all traffic lights, signs, and road markings.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Keep them straight and set the parking brake.
Turn them away from the curb.
Turn them toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels sharply to the left, away from the curb. If your brakes fail, your vehicle will roll into the curb instead of into traffic.

questions.question: Two drivers arrive at the same time at an open intersection. Who goes first?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver can go without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: At an open intersection, give the right-of-way to the driver on your right if you both arrive at the same time. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: People are walking on the road ahead.
A pedestrian crossing is ahead.
Pedestrians cannot cross here.
Watch for construction workers on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: A pedestrian crossing is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a pedestrian crossing is ahead. Drivers should be careful and watch for people who may be crossing.

questions.question: Which driving technique helps you avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?

options.text: Add weight to your vehicle for better grip.
Leave highways as fast as you can.
Use four-wheel drive.
Drive slower and stay farther behind other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower and stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: Slow down on snowy or icy roads. Driving slower and leaving more space between your car and the car in front of you are the best ways to avoid crashes.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and let pass:

options.text: Vehicles already in the roundabout.
Bicycles already in the roundabout.
People walking in the roundabout.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to all pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: What does a green arrow with a red light mean?

options.text: You can only go straight.
You can only drive in the direction of the arrow.
Wait for a solid green light to go in any direction.
All vehicles must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only drive in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you may only drive in the direction shown by the arrow if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: What should you do if you miss your exit on an interstate?

options.text: Stop and make a U-turn.
Exit at the next exit and come back to the one you missed.
Ask the driver next to you for help.
Back up on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit at the next exit and come back to the one you missed.
questions.explanation: Never back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Go to the next exit and turn around safely.

questions.question: What does a "No standing" sign mean?

options.text: You can never stop your car there.
You can park there if you stay in your car.
You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
You can stop to load or unload goods.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
questions.explanation: A "No standing" sign means you may only stop for a short time to pick up or drop off passengers.

questions.question: How do you stay out of a truck or bus driver's blind spot?

options.text: Never pass them.
Do not drive next to them and do not drive too close behind them.
Flash your lights.
Honk your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive next to them and do not drive too close behind them.
questions.explanation: Large trucks and buses have big blind spots on the sides and rear. Stay away from their sides and do not follow them too closely.

questions.question: What does an arrow painted on the road mean?

options.text: You may make the movement shown by the arrow if you choose to.
You must make the movement shown by the arrow only if traffic lights are broken.
You must stop before making the movement shown by the arrow.
You must make the movement shown by the arrow while following traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must make the movement shown by the arrow while following traffic signals.
questions.explanation: An arrow painted on the road shows which direction drivers in that lane must go. Follow all traffic signs and signals before moving in the direction of the arrow.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes going the same direction will soon become one lane. Drivers must merge safely.

questions.question: When can you use your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you have lost control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your car. This warns other drivers about the danger.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is an object on the road.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a sharp curve in the direction shown by the arrow. In this case, the road curves left. You may see several of these signs along a curve.

questions.question: ____ greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity.

options.text: High speeds
Slow speeds
Night driving
Uphill slopes

questions.correctAnswerText: High speeds
questions.explanation: High speeds greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity. The faster you drive, the harder your vehicle hits in a collision.

questions.question: When can you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When the train has passed.
Never.
When the lights stop flashing.
When other drivers do it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when warning signals appear. Warning signals include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a person signaling, or a train's horn. Never go around a lowered gate.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, what should you do?

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Get your documents ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
Get out and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel and ask passengers to keep their hands visible. Stay in your car unless the officer tells you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your driver license, registration, and insurance card.

questions.question: Two solid white lines mark a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know that:

options.text: Drivers have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show where pedestrians should cross safely. Crosswalks are marked with horizontal lines, vertical lines, or both. Always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.
